chunks: As for what Mūsā ibn al-Qāsim narrated from Ṣafwān, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abī Baṣīr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said:

The one performing tamattuʿ, when he has performed tawaf and saʿy, then recites the talbiyah before trimming the hair, then he may not trim the hair, and he no longer has mutʿah. So this report is to be understood as applying to one who did that deliberately; but if he did it forgetfully, then his ʿumrah is not invalidated, according to what the first report indicated, and this gives further clarification of that.

key_terms.سَعَى: performed saʿy between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah
key_terms.لَبَّى: recited the talbiyah for entering the state of pilgrimage rites
key_terms.مُتْعَةٌ: the state and ruling of tamattuʿ pilgrimage
key_terms.يُقَصِّرَ: to trim the hair as part of concluding the ʿumrah rites

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim in tamattuʿ recites the talbiyah before taqsir out of forgetfulness?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses a legal ruling concerning the pilgrim performing Hajj al-tamattuʿ who recites the talbiyah for hajj before doing taqsir after tawaf and saʿy. It clarifies that invalidation applies when this is done deliberately, whereas if it is done forgetfully, the ʿumrah remains valid.
